topic: Can we create an environmentally friendly replacement for plastics?
scientific_reframe: For a defined product function and service lifetime, when do bio-based or biodegradable polymers reduce life-cycle greenhouse-gas emissions, fossil-resource use, persistent pollution, and human-health burden relative to a conventional plastic, while retaining required mechanical, barrier, safety, and end-of-life performance?
primary_gap: Material labels and resin-level metrics do not identify when a replacement delivers equal service with lower total life-cycle harm.
recommended_direction: FUNCTIONAL-CIRCULAR-POLYMER: co-design polymer formulation, product function, and realistic end-of-life pathway.
required_boundaries: bio-based is not synonymous with biodegradable
biodegradable is not synonymous with home compostable or marine degradable
compare equal delivered service rather than equal mass
no candidate is declared environmentally superior before execution
